_about: Dispensa sample data — Mediterranean meal planner. Framework-agnostic. Attach this to a new chat so a new design variant starts from identical content. All pantry/'have'/cookable fields are believable PLACEHOLDER data (the real product doesn't track pantry yet).

categoryKey._note: The 7 quantitatively-tracked Mediterranean categories. This is the product's core colour system — reused identically on the weekly-balance panel, day chips, recipe badges, and Plan chips. Cooler hues = 'eat more', warmer = 'eat less'. ALWAYS pair colour with a text label or icon, never colour alone. 'dir': more = floor/target to reach, less = ceiling to stay under, mod = moderate band. Hex values are from a prior variant — a NEW variant should derive its own specific hues but keep these PROPERTIES (cool/warm split, light/dark/outline relationships, AA contrast).

fish.label: Fish & seafood
fish.rule: at least twice a week; aim for ≥1 oily fish

dailyBase._note: NOT counted in the weekly balance panel. Render as quiet, neutral, OUTLINED chips so they read as 'supporting'. Gentle daily reminders, not quotas.

plantBadge._note: Separate from BOTH the 7-colour key AND the neutral daily-base chips. Any recipe with diet 'veg' or 'vegan' gets ONE distinct leaf badge, in a palette colour that is NOT the legumes green (so it's never confused with legumes). Show on cards & Browse. NEVER appears in the weekly balance panel.

collections._note: A separate browsing dimension (how the user curated recipes over years). Warm neutral pill/cards with live counts — NOT the protein colour key. For the Browse screen (not built yet).

week._note: Sample planned week (June 16–22). Values are recipe ids. Wed is 'today'. Thu & Sun intentionally empty to show empty-state.

recipeFields._note: Field legend for the recipes array below.
recipeFields.title: recipe name (some intentionally Italian — keep accents)
recipeFields.tracks: array of { c: <categoryKey>, note?: 'oily' } — a recipe can count toward MORE THAN ONE tracked category (add to every one it touches)
recipeFields.cookable: PLACEHOLDER: mostly makeable from current stock ('Cookable now')
recipeFields.ing: ingredients: q=quantity (null=non-numeric), u=unit, n=name, have=in kitchen (placeholder)

recipes.title: Pasta e Ceci
recipes.desc: A brothy Roman soup of chickpeas and small pasta, scented with rosemary and good oil.
steps: Warm the oil and gently soften the garlic and rosemary, about 3 minutes.
Add passata and half the chickpeas; simmer 10 minutes.
Blend a ladleful smooth, return it for body, then add stock and pasta.
Cook until al dente, finish with a thread of raw oil and black pepper.

recipes.title: Orata all'Acqua Pazza
recipes.desc: Sea bream poached in "crazy water" — tomatoes, garlic, parsley and a splash of white wine.
steps: Sear garlic in oil, add halved tomatoes and let them slump.
Pour in wine, let it steam off, add a splash of water.
Lay in the fish, cover and poach 12–14 minutes, spooning broth over.
Scatter parsley and serve in shallow bowls with the broth.

recipes.title: Sgombro in Saor
recipes.desc: Venetian mackerel under sweet-sour onions — an oily fish that loves a night in the fridge.
steps: Fry the floured mackerel briefly, set aside.
Soften sliced onions slowly until sweet, add vinegar.
Layer fish and onions with raisins and pine nuts.
Rest at least overnight before serving at room temperature.

recipes.title: Zuppa di Lenticchie e Parmigiano
recipes.desc: Lentil soup finished with a melting rind of parmesan — counts twice toward your week.
steps: Sweat the diced soffritto in oil until soft.
Add lentils, the rind and water to cover; simmer 30 minutes.
Fish out the rind, season, and loosen with water if needed.
Serve with grated parmesan and a drizzle of oil.

recipes.title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.desc: Hunter’s chicken braised with tomato, rosemary and olives until the meat slips off the bone.
steps: Brown the chicken well on all sides; remove.
Deglaze with wine, add tomatoes, olives and rosemary.
Return chicken, cover and braise gently 35 minutes.
Reduce the sauce a little and rest before serving.

recipes.title: Lemon & Herb Roast Chicken
recipes.desc: A whole bird roasted over lemons and thyme — Sunday lunch that becomes three more meals.
steps: Rub the bird with oil, salt and lemon zest.
Stuff the cavity with halved lemons and thyme.
Roast at 200°C for 75–80 minutes, basting twice.
Rest 15 minutes before carving.

recipes.title: Frittata di Zucchine
recipes.desc: Soft courgette frittata with mint and a little pecorino — equally good warm or packed for lunch.
steps: Slice and soften the courgettes in oil until golden.
Beat eggs with pecorino, mint, salt and pepper.
Pour over the courgettes and cook low until almost set.
Finish under the grill and slide out to cool slightly.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.desc: Eggs poached in a spiced pepper and tomato sauce, scooped up with bread.
steps: Soften onion and peppers with cumin in oil.
Add tomatoes and simmer to a thick sauce.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook to taste.
Finish with herbs and serve from the pan.

recipes.title: Ribollita
recipes.desc: Tuscan "reboiled" bread and bean soup — thrifty, deep, and better the next day.
steps: Build a soffritto, add beans and chopped greens.
Simmer with water until everything is meltingly soft.
Tear in the bread and stir until it collapses into the soup.
Rest, reheat, and finish each bowl with raw oil.

recipes.title: Pumpkin & Sage Risotto
recipes.desc: Creamy risotto with roasted pumpkin, sage butter and parmesan.
steps: Roast diced pumpkin until caramelised.
Toast the rice with onion, then add stock a ladle at a time.
Fold through the pumpkin near the end.
Beat in parmesan and sage off the heat.

recipes.title: Bruschette ai Fagioli
recipes.desc: Grilled bread piled with white beans, garlic and rosemary oil — lunch in ten minutes.
steps: Warm the beans with rosemary oil and a little of their liquid.
Crush lightly to a rough, spoonable texture.
Grill the bread and rub with the cut garlic.
Pile on the beans, season, and finish with more oil.

recipes.title: Grilled Sardines
recipes.desc: Whole sardines over fire with lemon and oregano — the cheapest oily fish, and the best.
steps: Pat the sardines dry, oil and salt them well.
Grill hot, 2–3 minutes a side, until the skin blisters.
Squeeze over lemon and scatter oregano.
Serve at once with bread and a green salad.

recipes.title: Stufato di Manzo alle Olive
recipes.desc: Slow beef stew with olives and orange peel — a once-a-week treat, made lean.
steps: Brown the beef hard in batches.
Soften onions, deglaze with wine, add olives and peel.
Cover and braise low for two hours until tender.
Skim, season, and rest before serving.

recipes.title: Sausage & Lentil Stew
recipes.desc: A few good sausages stretched over a pot of lentils — comfort with a conscience.
steps: Brown the sausages and set aside.
Soften the vegetables, add lentils and tomatoes.
Nestle the sausages back in and simmer 30 minutes.
Slice the sausages through and season the lentils well.

recipes.title: Pasta alla Norma
recipes.desc: Sicilian pasta with fried aubergine, tomato and salted ricotta — summer on a plate.
steps: Fry the cubed aubergine until deep gold; drain.
Simmer passata with garlic and basil to a loose sauce.
Cook the pasta, toss with sauce and most of the aubergine.
Top with the rest and torn basil.

recipes.title: Focaccia alle Olive
recipes.desc: Dimpled, oil-pooled focaccia studded with olives — the table’s anchor.
steps: Mix a wet dough and let it rise until doubled.
Stretch into an oiled tin and dimple deeply.
Press in olives, drizzle with oil and brine.
Bake hot until golden and crisp at the edges.

mediterraneanEngine._note: How the balance logic works. A recipe contributes to EVERY category in its 'tracks' array. The weekly balance panel counts servings per category and flags over (red/processed) / under (fish, legumes). 'Fills a gap' suggests unplaced recipes whose tracks cover the most-under category. Serving ≈ a palm / ~130g cooked legumes / ~100–150g fish or meat. All targets editable on Goals & Profile (not built yet).

scalingModes.byServings: stepper rescales every quantity proportionally off recipe.serves
scalingModes.byIngredient: user types the amount they actually have for ONE ingredient; everything rescales off that ratio (ratio = typedAmount / ing.q). This is the more-used mode for shop-first cooking.
